drafted_from: tool:list-resend-webhooks's own row (tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json: its words, input schema and sample run) and test/list-resend-webhooks.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Which addresses does my Resend account send its email events to, and is each one on?", naming the held key, {"key_name": "resend-api-key-of-my-shop"}. It runs tool:list-resend-webhooks and answers {"webhooks":[{"id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000011","url":"https://example.com/webhooks/mail","status":"enabled","events":["email.delivered","email.bounced","email.complained"]}],"count":1}
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads the webhooks your email-sending account has and writes nothing.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once, so its key is held in your vault under a name of yours (a key with full access: a sending-only key cannot read webhooks). The key is never typed into the request.
2. Say to your AI: "List my Resend webhooks", and give the held key's name. It calls tools:run with tool tool:list-resend-webhooks and {"key_name": "<that name>"}.
3. Read what comes back: each webhook's id, its address (url), its state (enabled or disabled) and the events it sends, and how many there are. A webhook's signing secret and the key are never shown.
4. A webhook that reads disabled has stopped sending: its address failed for too long. Fix what answers at its address first, then switch it on again at the provider.

worked_examples.title: Two webhooks, one switched off
worked_examples.ask: List my Resend webhooks and say which are on.
worked_examples.given: The row's sample run: GET https://api.resend.com/webhooks answering two made-up webhooks. Ids and addresses are synthetic.
